name: Screen orientation
plain: Whether the screen is portrait or landscape and its rotation angle.
meaning: Shows how a phone is held and whether a tablet is docked. Reports type (portrait-primary etc.) and angle 0, 90, 180 or 270; changes with a rotate event.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can tell if your screen is upright or sideways, and by how many degrees
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads or you rotate the device.
can: Notice when you rotate the device
cannot: See the device's tilt or movement, which is a different sensor
Learn how you are holding the device when rotation is locked

story.what_it_is: Tells a page whether your screen is tall or wide, and how far it is turned.

marketing.name: Screen Orientation API
marketing.pitch: Explains how a page can read whether the screen is portrait or landscape and react when it turns.

story.for_you: You turn your phone and the page rearranges itself. That change is the page reading the orientation and moving things around.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to fit layouts to the screen shape. It also hints at the device type, since a laptop is always wide and a phone often tall.

use_cases.example: A browser racing game switches to a wide track and moves the buttons to the sides when you turn the phone.
A video site goes full screen when you turn your phone sideways.
A store shows a two column gallery in landscape and a single scroll in portrait.
A web map shows a side panel in landscape and a bottom sheet in portrait.
A fraud check notes that a supposed phone never changes orientation and reports a desktop size, a sign of a faked device.
A reading app asks students to turn the device so long math tables fit.
A team sees which orientation most visitors use before designing a new page.

linkedin.how: Orientation collected. Read by the LinkedIn APFC fingerprint script (alleged by BrowserGate, partly confirmed by BleepingComputer).
